title: RED FLAG ALARM — HYPOTHETICAL EXAMPLE
description: Demo showing all 7 red flags triggered for educational purposes

flags.explanation: Promoter has pledged 42.5% of shares — above 20% threshold. High pledging signals financial stress and forced-selling risk.
Reported profit ₹320Cr but operating cash flow is ₹-850Cr. Negative OCF with positive profit suggests aggressive accrual accounting.
Receivables grew 45% while revenue grew only 10% — receivables growing 4.5× faster than revenue. Classic sign of channel stuffing or collection issues.
Debt/Equity ratio 4.20 — above 2× threshold. High leverage risk.
Interest coverage 0.80× — company cannot cover interest from operating profit. Extreme distress.
Promoter holding fallen consecutively for 3 quarters. Current: 38.2% vs 3 quarters ago: 48.5% (Δ -10.3%). Sustained promoter selling is a significant red flag.
Auditor changed in FY26 annual report — new auditor appointed mid-year without clear explanation. Prior auditor served 12 years.

disclaimer: ALL DATA IS HYPOTHETICAL AND FOR EDUCATIONAL DEMONSTRATION ONLY. Not real financial data.
